These are genetics originally from John Hummer's collection. John collected divisions of the plants before the site was destroyed, and these are seedlings from his divisions. They are certainly very similar to Barry's seed grown plants, but quite different in the sense that they tend to be taller and more slender. I found one individual that had one trap with red veins, and on the same plant, another trap without any red veins.

posts.body_html: Here are some more summer pitchers. I like the fact that John Hummer's genetics gets taller than my other Hurricane Creek whites originally from Barry Rice. The shape is also pretty nice as well, and is rather different. It'll be interesting to see if these produce extremely solid white pitchers in the fall-fingers crossed.

posts.body_html:
Finally, here's John Hummer's hurricane creek whites all grown out. I was going to toss them at one point but it turns out they're actually pretty nice. This just goes to show if you have a plant that doesn't look all that great at first, don't toss it because that might just be environmental conditions. Of course, most of you wouldn't throw away what I would, but you eventually will once your collection gets out of control:



Not bad at all, and these are quite vigorous:

Be careful MW, very careful.... If you lose the discipline to be discerning and throw things out you'll end up like my buddy Don Gray who NEVER gets rid of anything. Hence, he's the only person on the poll results so far To what degree is your obsession....? to register as having 5000+ plants. Believe me, the total is around 7000!

The number of Sarras one has to manage ( )can jump up and bite you on the butt before you realise it.....

Jokes aside, you did have a instinctively discerning eye though - that is a very pleasing clone with lovely balance. Definitely a keeper
